utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. There's just a few last-minute matters to attend to, if Your Honours please. As I said yesterday, there's some documentation relating to exchange lists. Ms. Reidy will address you on that and then I have a few other matters to deal with and then I'll go after her. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the situation with exchange lists is that on the exhibit list, the Prosecutor's Exhibit list filed with their pre-trial brief on the 9th of April last year, at E1 and E2 of that list were a number of -- two sets of exchange records running into several hundred pages each, one set, E1, was a set of records that the Office of the Prosecutor had received from a Croat source, and E2 were a set of exchange records received from Serb sources. What we are seeking to do now is to have entered into evidence several of those lists from what was E2 on the exhibit list, that is a Serb-sourced exchange list, but not all of them. And the reason that we're not seeking to have the whole of them entered into evidence is that we have sat with Defence counsel and gone through some of the documents. Some are illegible, so they would have little probative value, and others lack a signature or clear identification of authorship, and those we've agreed would not at this stage be entered fully into evidence. So these were documents which in fact are covered by Judge Robinson's pre-trial order on admission of documents, and they do fall in the Prosecutor's Exhibit list. What they are, it's 102 pages, and that consists of 41 exchange lists, dating -- the first one dates from the 25th of June, 1992, and the last list chronologically we have is the 15th of September, 1993. The lists do cover exchanges from a wider area than just Bosanski Samac, but they do form part of the Prosecution evidence to show for the Prosecution to establish the context and general pattern into which these exchanges fell. So I would like to move to have these entered fully into evidence. As I said, they amount to 41 lists and just over a hundred pages. I don't know how one would propose to have them numbered, whether to give the whole batch what used to be E2 a single exhibit number and then subnumbers, depending on the dates for each list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. And would Your Honours like me to submit all 40 lists then individually or en masse and then I can submit to the registry an index just of each date that we have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think it would be easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think that's probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Much easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The best way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will take less time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would Your Honour like me to give to the registry now the set of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that we can have the common number dictated and then the sublisting can be done later.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've provided five sets. The other sets of these documents for Defence counsel I will place in Defence counsel's locker. I approached them before this and explained that in court I only have five at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to take advantage of this bit of time while the usher was distributing these documents to say that we do not object to these documents being introduced. In fact, these documents were provided to us during the pre-trial period. We verified these documents and compared them with the Prosecution, and we accept that they be admitted as -- that they be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be P146. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then the subdivisions will be done by the Prosecution as already explained?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely. I'll file that this afternoon once we've risen, the index. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Then the next batch, if any?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one more matter that perhaps I should address. It's the filing of the redacted version of Witness O's 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And again, I have copies. Your Honours, just for the record, what has been passed to the usher is the version of Witness O's 92 bis statement that appeared as annex B to the confidential motion. It is in the English language, and the redaction of the B/C/S version is just being verified with the translators at the moment, and I hope it could be filed also by the time we rise from this session. But that is the motion -- that is the statement as was filed as annex B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right. It already has a number, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Any other documents? That's all. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, there remain some documents that are still only marked for identification, and if I may, I'd like to deal with some of those. Registry very helpfully gave me a list of those documents. First is P30 ID. That is an architectural drawing of the primary school. It was a drawing produced by Mr. Zecevic, and it was referred to during the evidence of one of the Bicic brothers, Muhamed. Mr. Weiner produced the drawing to the witness. The witness went on -- placed the document on the ELMO and then, if you read the transcript, went on to describe various aspects of the situation in the primary school by reference to the drawing. It seems that, for whatever reason, it wasn't fully entered into evidence at that stage, but I can see no reason why, having seen the transcript, that it should not be fully admitted into evidence, and I'd ask that it be given that status, that it be fully admitted into evidence. That's P 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see no objection from the Defence. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. There's no objection. Can we have it confirmed that it will retain the same numbers as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This will be P30 and P30 ter. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. The next item is P33 ID and the corresponding B/C/S exhibit. That is a statement of Ibrahim Salkic. It arose in this way: He was -- it was produced in re-examination. He had been cross-examined extensively by Mr. Zecevic and Mr. Pantelic regarding previous statements that he had made and other documents that were, for want of a better description, unsigned statements that he had made. I was attempting to establish which statements were his signed, adopted, fully completed, official statements, and I therefore, in re-examination produced to him a 1995 statement, which was his fully adopted, fully signed statement, the English statement. The purpose of producing that was merely to establish which of his statements were adopted and signed by him and which weren't, and that is the only purpose of that particular document. So I would seek to produce it fully into evidence merely to establish that limited point, not to establish the contents of it or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Any objection from the Defence? I can see none. Can we have confirmation of the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It will be P33 and P33 ter. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: The next document, I wonder if I might have an opportunity to just briefly look at it. It's P47. It should be a Red Cross document, Red Cross card. It arose in the evidence of Esad Dagovic. Yes. That document was relevant to showing his movements out of Croatia to Europe, long after his release from the camps in Bosanski Samac. I can see no reason why it should not be fully admitted into evidence. There's no translation requirements because the document is already translated. It's got both B/C/S and English side by side, so it's understandable at a glance and doesn't needed translation. And if you're to understand his evidence fully, then it seems to me that it should go into evidence fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have confirmation of the number, please, as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It will be P47 ter and P47. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Next document that is only identified as P59 ID. This was an extensive list of Croat and Muslim names of people from Bosanski Samac. It's been marked for identification at this stage. Having read the transcript, there were concerns from the Bench, and indeed from the Prosecution, regarding the ability to prove its authenticity. Nothing has changed since that time, and I would ask that it remain merely identified at this stage. Nothing has changed since the document was first produced in court to improve its status as an ID document, so that should simply remain. It may be that further evidence will arise in the course of the Defence case that may shed further light on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. If it's just marked for identification, then it doesn't form part of the evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: I appreciate that, but I would ask that it remain marked for identification. There is a further document, P84 ID. This was a document that arose during the course of the evidence of Mr. Todorovic. It's a document that he could not read because the copy was so bad. I indicated that I did not intend to produce it into evidence. It was marked for identification merely to -- for an abundance of caution. It should remain merely marked for identification at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. MR. DI FAZIO: And the same applies to P128 ID. There is again nothing that has changed in evidential terms since that document was first produced warranting its full admission, so I ask that that remain as is, namely, simply marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: As far as P67 is concerned, issues were raised yesterday regarding that particular document. I persist in my application to have P67 fully admitted. It is, in fact, as far as I can tell, an exact copy of the same document as P13 and P13 ter. That was admitted during the evidence of Sulejman Tihic early on in the case. He commented upon that particular document. It is the same document, as I can see, as D50/3, which was produced by the Defence. So P13 and D50/3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Are, as far as I can tell, one and the same document essentially. We introduced it first through the evidence of Sulejman Tihic. The Defence later introduced it again as D50/3. Then Mr. Fitozovic gave evidence and produced another document, which is essentially the same document but differs in several respects in that it has stamps on it and a signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the one marked -- MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. My apologies. My apologies. My apologies. It differs in the sense that it has handwritten numbers on it, no signature, and no stamp, unlike P13 and D50/3. So P67 is, to that extent, a different document, and he also commented on its authenticity. You recall that he produced it, as Ms. Reidy pointed out to you yesterday. So it's a document that should go into evidence, in my submission, P67, because it differs from the other two, P13 and D50/3, and because he provided that commentary regarding P67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Any objection? Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I said that I would give you a clarification today, and I think that the Prosecution will agree with me. We can agree on some things. What I can tell you right away is that the document D67, which was an ID so far, should be admitted into evidence, based on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: P.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So on behalf of the Defence, I can hereby inform you that all of us agree for that document to be fully admitted. What further complicates the issue is the relationship between the documents D -- P53 [As interpreted] and P13. Those are not identical documents. They're not identical to P67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the correct numbers? Are you discussing D50/3?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would ask the registry to assist us and provide the original of the document P67, the original of D50/3, and document P13. At a first glance, they look like identical documents, but they are not, and this is where the problem lies. Let me first tell you something about P67. This is a non-contentious document. Mr. Fitozovic said, regarding this document, that it was his document, that he had it on him when he swam across Sava River, and that that document, if you remember, that was not signed. When I showed to Mr. Fitozovic document D50/3, which was also an original, it was not a photocopy, it was an original with a signature - so when I showed this document to him, he said that that document was a forgery because he had an original of that document. And that is why this document which we identified as D50/3 had an ID designation so that we could, during the Defence case, be able to provide that that document was an authentic one. By conducting further verification, I was able to establish that this document, D50/3 ter, had been previously introduced and admitted as the Prosecution's document and was marked as P13. That document had a seal and a signature. Mr. Tihic, on the 17th of September, when asked by Mr. Di Fazio, on pages 1355 to 1357, confirmed that that document was an authentic one and that it had been signed by an authorised person from the SDA party. So we don't have a problem with P67 any more. However, the problem is that document P13 is in fact a copy of D50/3 ter, and this is why I am now asking that the document D50/3 be admitted into evidence and not exist as an ID document, so that we now have a unified designation for this document, because, as I am saying, documents P13 and document D50/3 are identical ones. P13 was introduced by the Prosecution and was provided to the Prosecution by the Defence of Mr. Zaric. This is the same document offered by the Defence as the document D50/3. I hope I was clear enough. And let me just give another clarification so that there are no misunderstandings. It was very frequent in the administrative proceedings in those times that there were several copies of the same documents, and this was confirmed by Mr. Tihic during his testimony, on page 1357. He, Mr. Tihic, at that time confirmed that Mr. Fitozovic was the author of that document, and I don't think that this is a contentious issue at all. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, just may I briefly reply? I've got no problem with D50/3 being given a full evidentiary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Exhibit number. MR. DI FAZIO: Full exhibit number, but that's as far as I go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: There are a lot of other matters, factual allegations raised by my learned friend that I don't want to be seen to be agreeing to simply because I don't object to D50/3 going fully into evidence. For example, the assertion that Tihic agreed that Fitozovic was the author. He said it was probably Alija Fitozovic or somebody else. Whoever made it did it in the spirit of the policy that we are pursuing. So there's a lot of unclarity about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But in any case, as far as admission is concerned, we can have them admitted. It will remain up to the Trial Chamber as to how much weight it attaches to each of these documents when analysing the evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, exactly. May I just confer briefly with my colleague, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Weiner suggests - I don't know if it will help the Court and registry - that there be some sort of cross-reference in the exhibit list so that we can easily see that D50/3, P13, and P67 are said to be essentially one and the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, I don't think that should be done. They should just retain their numbers as they are. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then each party can discuss them and demonstrate how useful they are and persuade the Trial Chamber to accept their own interpretation of the contents or the status of the document. So could we just have confirmation that P67 will retain its number and D50/3 will be an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Both P67 and P67 ter will be admitted into evidence, and D50/3 and D50/3 ter will be admitted into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Any other matters? Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender certain translations of the exhibits that had already been admitted. I'm now referring to five exhibits. The first one is D15/3. I have received an official translation into English, and now I would like to ask the usher to distribute this document. The witness during whose testimony this document was offered I think was Witness L, if I'm not mistaken. It should probably be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution is aware of this -- [Microphone not activated]. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I haven't had a chance to examine the documents carefully, if Your Honours please, but if these are translations of exhibits then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: From what Mr. Lukic says, maybe we can confirm with the registry whether we have D15/3.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is correct. D15/3 ter was admitted under the testimony of Witness L and is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is D18/3, also marked as an ID document, and it is also a document written by Witness L and sent to the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Might I ask that we conduct this exercise on some other occasion? I'm almost a hundred per cent certain that what Mr. Lukic says about the admissibility of these documents is true and correct. I would just like an opportunity to look at the documents myself and examine them and make sure that there is just nothing more than a translation issue. We could deal with it on the next occasion that we meet. That will give me an opportunity to go through them and I can say -- save time by simply saying that I've looked at all of this. We have no objection. They can simply be admitted and fully exhibited. Would that not be a quicker way of doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: When you talk of when we next meet, when do you mean? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I propose to go on and close the Prosecution case today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So I was thinking that maybe what you needed was -- is a break. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, we could -- if you were minded to give us a break, we could check through these documents fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, you didn't give the translated copies to the Prosecution before now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honours. It is my mistake. I've had these translations on me for quite a long time and I was looking for a good opportunity to tender them. These are simply translations, and I believe that nothing was contentious regarding them. And we can tell you now which documents they are, and then perhaps the Prosecution can, after the break, give their position as to whether they oppose this or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you go through and then we'll have a break and allow the Prosecution to state their position. But the Trial Chamber has always given instructions that please, as early as possible, do serve copies of documents to the other party so we don't have this type of problem. All right. You can run through them, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is D18/3. It's a letter written by Witness L to this Tribunal. The following document is D49/3. It's an exchange list dated 18 September 1992. The next document is D51/3 ter, marked as an ID document. It's a letter dated 4th of June, 1992, a letter written by Marko Bozovic, commander of the newly established Territorial Defence of Samac. And this document was also tendered during the testimony of Mr. Fitozovic. Another document that has been marked as an ID document, but not only due to the lack of translation but also because authenticity was brought into question. I now have a translation of this document, but I'm not going to ask that it be admitted fully into evidence right now. The document I'm speaking of is D66/3 ter ID. We had it only partially translated, and now I have a full translation. It was a letter of guarantee, and this was brought out during the testimony of Jelena Kapetanovic. She claimed not to know anything about this document. I'm now providing just the translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the translation that you mentioned, it's on the record letter dated 4th of June, 1992. It's actually -- the document I received is dated 16th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will verify what is stated in the transcript, but the date should be the 16th of April, because that was when the TO was established, Territorial Defence, and this is when the letter was written and sent to Sarajevo. Your Honours, I have two more questions that I wanted to bring up. One of them relates to a request of Defence to allow them to have access to documentation used by Mrs. Ewa Tabeau when preparing her report. When I approached you with this request, pursuant to Rule 67 of the Rules of Evidence, you instructed us to resolve this matter with the other side, with the Prosecution. Following your instructions, the Defence and the Prosecution held the meeting, at which time Defence asked that our expert be given access to the database used by Mrs. Tabeau. I will remind you that during her testimony she had told us that she had used two databases. One was the one obtained from the statistics bureau of Sarajevo, relating to the census of population in 1991, and the other database was the one given to her by the OSCE, and it pertains to the list of voters in 1997. And this issue came up, if you remember, when we spoke about identification. After obtaining general permission to verify this, we were informed by the Prosecution that they were unable to give these documents to us because, as they told us, they were confidential documents, documents obtained from both of the sources I mentioned. I have to tell you that not only for the Defence, but for this case in its entirety, these facts are very important, because the entire expert report of Mrs. Tabeau was based on this information, and this is something that can be also important for the work of our expert witness. What is of a special importance to the Defence is that based on the law on census which was in force in 1991, the census and all of the documents relating to the census are considered confidential and can only be used for the purposes of the census. We are unable to obtain this information because this is not public information. However, in the interests of Defence, this is something that we need to verify, this information, and we are of the opinion that if the Prosecution is able to obtain this information, then there must be a way that this information, if necessary, pursuant to the Court's order, could be put at the disposal of the Defence. So this is the database used by the computer software, as was explained to us by Mrs. Tabeau, and this is something that the Prosecution has. So we just wanted to inform the Trial Chamber that the parties were unable to reach an agreement and have this information delivered to the Defence. We believe that this is not something -- this is not the material that can be considered in the light of Rule 70, and if this information is withheld from the Defence, then this would severely impede our work. I have another question I wanted to bring up, but perhaps we should discuss this matter first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's hear from the Prosecution on the availability of this material. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps Ms. Reidy should address you on this. I dealt with this issue in its initial stages, but later in the month she took over the matter, and I think she is probably in a better position to inform you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. What I can advise the Bench of is my discussions with Ms. Tabeau, and yes, indeed, how the Office of the Prosecutor was entitled to have access to the information contained in the databases. The information is Rule 70 information insofar as it was given to the Office of the Prosecutor on a confidential basis, purely for the purposes of the Office of the Prosecutor to generate further evidence. As counsel for Mr. Tadic has said, the nature of this information being census information is, even in his own domestic jurisdiction, and my jurisdiction, confidential. It obviously contains a lot of personal, potentially sensitive information, and it's not something that we are in a position to disclose to other parties, given the circumstances in which it was made available to the Office of the Prosecutor. To that extent, I think the information, the sort of information they're looking for, does fall clearly under Rule 70. I appreciate from the Defence case that they would, of course, like to be able to inspect this documentation, and when I spoke with Defence counsel, there may be a way around it, through special protection orders, with a Court order, through -- I don't know whether Defence counsel have attempted to approach the sources themselves, but we cannot ourselves pass over that information, the raw data which we got, which we were given on a strictly confidential basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. When Mr. Lukic was making his submissions, I was wondering about the steps the Defence have taken, and also wondering about disclosure with restrictions, protective measures and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would you like to hear the Defence or the Prosecution respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to find out from the Defence, before you finish, Ms. Reidy, whether they had made any approaches to the authorities who have got this information in their custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I may address the Court with some details with regard to this issue. The Defence is of the opinion that in this particular case the fact of the possession of certain materials by the Prosecution is actually the subject that we have to discuss. The fact that the Prosecution is in possession of software; number 2, census, some result of census of 1991 in Bosnia-Herzegovina; and number 3, the voters list specifically for municipality of Samac. We think that it is not in accordance with the spirit of the Rule, particularly Rule 70, that facts and voters list for municipality of Samac has anything with the new evidence or ongoing investigation or whatever. We are focused specifically on the population of municipality of Samac, and Odzak as well, because that is actually the subject-matter of the indictment. And specifically, for this population, we want to make certain additional analysis by our expert to compare, to give her or his opinion with regard to municipality of Samac and Odzak. In the interests of justice, it is absolutely, I think, appropriate for our expert to come here, at the premises of the Prosecution, in the Office of the Prosecution, in the presence of Prosecution expert Mrs. Tabeau, to discuss the matter, to check the data, relevant data for this particular case, and to finish her or his expert report for this Trial Chamber. If we shall follow the suggestions of the Prosecution, then we have to go and to waste enormous time through OSCE organisation, government of Bosnia, by the way of judicial assistance of this Trial Chamber, and then maybe we shall come into the situation not to finish this case in total due to these reasons. Let me respectfully remind this Trial Chamber that to some extent similar situation we also got in this particular case when the Trial Chamber -- I believe it was Honourable Judges Robinson, Hunt, and Bennouna were in Pre-Trial stage first, with certain confidential documents in possession of Prosecution, confidential agreement between Office of the Prosecutor and NATO SHAPE. I think S-H-A-P-E is the abbreviation of this Supreme Command of NATO in Brussels. Finally, after long discussions, the Prosecution provided Defence with this confidential agreement. So based on this practice, on the previous practice, in handling of confidential documents, of course I think that following the protective measures, obligation of our expert not to disclose to the third parties everything what is done here, and all other necessary measures which this Trial Chamber deems necessary is actually available to all of us. So I respectfully ask this Trial Chamber to -- in also -- given the fact of the principle of equality of arms and the rights of the accused to a fair trial, to follow all of these principles and to grant our request with regard to the specific and isolated inspection of the facts of statistical data regarding municipality Bosanski Samac and Odzak. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I doubt if the Prosecution wish to reply to that. I think it's all clear from the initial submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: With respect, I would like to reply, because in that five-minute submission on the history of this case, Mr. Pantelic didn't actually advise us whether or not any steps were taken just to see whether or not they would be allowed access to that documentation, and he talks about fair trial, et cetera. I'm afraid that in the discussions that I had, particularly with Mr. Lukic, we made clear that this material is Rule 70, and we are bound by that Rule, as is the Chamber, which says that if we are in possession of information which has been provided to the Prosecutor on a confidential basis and which has been used solely for the purpose of generating new evidence, the initial information and its origin shall not be disclosed by the Prosecutor without the consent of the person or entity providing the initial information and shall, in any event, not be given in evidence without prior disclosure to the accused. And the second part of that involves disclosure and evidence. But we are not in a position off our own bat to disclose that evidence. We are, of course, happy to enter into discussions about what sort of protective measures could be provided for the information to go back to the source-giver and try to elicit their consent in the context of the Defence case and what sort of access they need and how that information would be used. But our position was that we cannot give that permission because, as Rule 70 information, it is the source provider who is the Guardian of that confidential information who has that right. So as I said, I don't -- the other -- when this -- this has arisen in other cases with confidential sources. I believe, for example, there had been ECMM reports, which are confidential, which the Office of the Prosecutor has had access to, and there have been possibly - I'm not so sure of this - potentially Red Cross documentation that there has been access to which is confidential. And on each occasion, I believe the Defence has approached those organisations initially of their own initiative, and if there has then been a problem, we try to find some negotiation. So I don't think that Mr. Pantelic's approach is necessarily very helpful. We will try to resolve this problem within the confines of Rule 70, and it would be helpful to know whether the Defence have taken any steps to know if they could get access to the sources quoted in Ms. Tabeau's expert report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think this is a matter which is quite separate from the course of the proceedings, because it relates to the preparation of the expert -- the evidence which the Defence wish to produce for their case, in support of their case. So let's go back to the Prosecution case. Are there any other matters, any documents outstanding? On this matter which has been raised, the Trial Chamber will give its ruling later. MR. DI FAZIO: No, there aren't any other matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we have these documents which have just been given in which the Prosecution wish to look at during the break. MR. DI FAZIO: The Defence documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Defence documents, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, we can look at those during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: During the break, and then be able to state their position. I just want to go back to the matter that was raised in July, just the last day before our break, dealing with the evidence which the Prosecution decided to exclude. Mr. Pantelic made submissions which amounted to a motion. In fact, he did say that. He wanted to have the witnesses called for cross-examination, notwithstanding the fact that their evidence was no longer required by the Prosecution and that it wouldn't be on record. I just want to make it clear that the Trial Chamber did decide that these witnesses wouldn't be called for cross-examination because the transcripts of their evidence have been excluded from the record, so there is no basis for cross-examination. And also to advise the Defence that if they wished to call any of these witnesses who are no longer required by the Prosecution, they can go ahead and do so. The other matter I wanted to raise was that since the fifth indictment was served, we haven't had a formal plea to the charges in the fifth amended indictment. So I just wanted to confirm with the accused persons that they retain their pleas of not guilty on all the charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think we will give time to the Defence counsel to confer, and also, just as much time as the Prosecution wish to look at the documents, and then when we come back we can finalise that and perhaps the Prosecution can decide whether or not to close their case. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I understand, we shall take a short break now. Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then, if you allow me, Your Honours, I would like to submit one oral motion to this Trial Chamber which we could deal during the break. It's appropriate time. There is a quite -- well, I cannot say whether it's with grounds or not, certain impressions of the Defence during the -- this trial proceedings that a certain number of Prosecution witnesses, whilst in The Hague, in groups of two, three, or four, following the transcripts and after the analysis of transcripts, we think that there are quite strange similarities with certain details in their testimonies, and therefore I respectfully move this Trial Chamber with the following motion: I would like, on behalf of Defence, and also in the presence of one of the members of our learned friends from the Prosecution, and also in assistance with Mr. Usher or the other person designated by this Trial Chamber, to inspect, very shortly inspect, in one minute or so, room 1002, which is just behind this courtroom, to see whether there are equipments, video or TV equipments there, where normally the Prosecution witnesses are, so to see whether they're able to follow the proceedings and to see what are the topics in proceedings. If we could do that, and to cover that matter during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You are through with your oral motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm finished with my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is there any response from the Prosecution? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I'm not aware of there being any video equipment in there, but -- and as far as the Prosecution is concerned, we've got no problem with that. But the only thing is it seems to be the province of the Victims and Witnesses Unit. I don't know if we would be treading on toes, on their toes, if we simply said yes, go in and inspect the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. I just wanted to know whether or not they have anything -- the Prosecution have anything to say about that. You don't have to -- MR. DI FAZIO: No, there's no video equipment, no tracking equipment, there's no TV screens. Yes. As Mr. Weiner points out, Victims and Witnesses Unit people, with the witnesses at all times, it's a waiting room, that place. It's a waiting room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then. Very well, then. We shall take a half-hour break and the Trial Chamber will give its ruling to the oral motion and the other matter raised, and the Trial Chamber expects the Prosecution to complete their submissions on the Defence documents. We'll take our break now and resume our proceedings at 10 to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber would like to find out from the accused persons on whether or not they maintain their pleas of not guilty to the fifth amended indictment. We will ask Dr. Blagoje Simic. You still maintain your pleas of not guilty to all the charges against you in the fifth amended indictment? THE ACCUSED SIMIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Miroslav Tadic. THE ACCUSED TADIC: [Interpretation] I believe that the Prosecution has proved that I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you maintain your plea of not guilty. Mr. Simo Zaric? THE ACCUSED TADIC: [Interpretation] Not guilty. [Realtime transcript indicated "THE ACCUSED ZARIC"]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. You can sit down. Yes. I have the response from Mr. Zaric in the -- on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that those were the words pronounced by Mr. Tadic, not Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could be of some assistance, actually, Mr. Zaric hasn't said anything. That was actually Mr. Tadic who said not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. I received it late, I think. Very well. Mr. Zaric, then. THE ACCUSED ZARIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll maintain the pleas of not guilty on all the charges in the fifth amended indictment. On the matters raised by the Defence regarding the sources of materials used by Dr. Tabeau, this is a separate matter which will not affect whether or not the Prosecution case can close today. It is a matter regarding the preparation of the Defence case for their expert witness in the relevant -- on the relevant matters raised by Dr. Tabeau. The Trial Chamber, at the moment, feels that the Defence should approach the relevant authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina and obtain the materials. If that does not succeed, then the Defence can make their relevant application to the Trial Chamber, and this must be done as quickly as possible so that it doesn't hold up the Defence case in the long run of the trial. On the oral motion by Mr. Pantelic regarding the room, the status of the room where the witnesses, the Prosecution witnesses, wait before coming into the courtroom, the Trial Chamber finds no basis for the inspection of the witness room. The fact that the evidence of Prosecution witnesses is similar is no basis for such an inspection, because it is clear that most of the witnesses were detained in the same places, received the similar treatment, hence their evidence which, according to the Defence is similar, and they haven't even given details of the similarities which, in their view, may be unusual. So the motion is dismissed. So we go back to the Prosecution on the Defence exhibits. What is their position? MR. DI FAZIO: No objection, if Your Honours please, to 15/3, 18/3, 49/3, 51/3, and we agree that 66/3 should remain merely marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have confirmation that the said documents will retain the same numbers as exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. They will become exhibits and retain the same numbers as previously given. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Back to the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. May the Prosecution close its case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Now that the case for the Prosecution has closed, the Trial Chamber has got a tentative schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I do apologise myself. Maybe it's appropriate moment, of course, according to your approval --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- to discuss or to introduce the issue with regard to the exhibits of Mr. Milan Simic. If I remember well, there was a suggestion of Trial Chamber about the admitted exhibits of -- and evidence on behalf of Mr. Milan Simic which might be of relevance for the other three defendants to maybe be admitted as -- on behalf of one of the co-accused, and maybe it's appropriate moment to have an approach and ruling on that. In fact, if Ms. Registrar can confirm. According to my list here, on behalf of Mr. Milan Simic, we have in total the last enumeration of the exhibit is D40/2. So in total it's about 40 exhibits. Following the instruction of this Trial Chamber, it was months ago, I think, we decided to accept some of these exhibits, because they're related to the work of municipality of Samac and all other details. So maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what you are saying is you are going to rely on them?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the other question might be how we shall, during the proceedings, make reference to them. Do we need now another enumeration, numbering, or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We shall retain the same numbers, to avoid confusion. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I made the review. There are certain -- for example, sketches or some witness statements specifically related to Mr. Milan Simic, and we don't want to rely to them. Just for the record, maybe it's five or six these exhibits. Maybe I can make --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe you can enumerate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, we are speaking -- Defence would not like to rely on the Exhibit D5/2, then D6/2, D7/2, D10/2, D20/2, D21/2, D31/2, and D41/2. And I just have a note that in fact there are 43 exhibits because according to the exhibit list which was updated on 31st of May this year, in total I got the information that it was 40. So maybe, Ms. Registrar -- I have also -- yes. And then D -- sorry. Yes. D42/2. Just a confirmation from the registrar about the Exhibit D41/2 and D42. Are they some kind of sketches or design?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps the registry can help us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the exhibit list is updated up to the 22nd of July, 2002. D41/2 is a diagram of the gym, and has been marked. It was marked by Witness N. D42/2 is another diagram, and it was marked by witness Dragan Delic. And D43/2 is an affidavit of witness Jankovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Probably it was related to the -- yes, I know. So to conclude, we don't want to rely on Exhibits D41/2, D42/2, and D43/2. In the remaining proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And that is common to both Mr. Lukic's and Mr. Lazarevic, all three.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is on behalf of all three of the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, with respect, I don't understand quite what is happening here. My friend keeps saying he doesn't want to rely on them. That's fine. He doesn't have to rely on them. But they're still evidence in the case, are they not? It's evidence, documentary evidence, that was produced to the Tribunal in the course of case number IT 95-9. I understand that they may not be of any use to the Defence and the Defence may not be interested in them. The Prosecution may wish to rely upon it, though, at some later stage if they become relevant. Is this an application to remove them from the evidentiary record? I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think -- yes, you can complete. MR. DI FAZIO: Our position firmly is is that it's all evidence in the case. Now, if it is of no use to the Defence and they don't wish to rely on it, fine. That might be the case with any number of documents. But I am concerned that we don't go any further than this and that we don't try to remove it from the evidentiary record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the confusion arises from the fact that these cases were separated after some evidence has been led. MR. DI FAZIO: Sure. I have no problem with that. Whatever evidence was used in the case of Mr. Simic thereafter, after the separation of the cases, fine, but up until that point, that was evidence that you heard, evaluated, and will be in a position to evaluate at the end of the case. And so for that point of view, I, as I said, I have no problem at all if the Defence want to put their cards on the table, so to speak, and make clear what they're relying on. However, our position firmly is that evidence, once admitted, remains evidence in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which is -- sorry, Your Honour. May I reply in brief?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which is of course not the position of the Defence. Our understanding of the ruling of this Trial Chamber was: Once the case against Mr. Milan Simic was separated, after the relevant decision of this Trial Chamber, all evidences, and there are, I believe, some discussion that in the transcripts, all evidences related to Mr. Milan Simic were, I would say, separated from the rest of proceedings against three co-accused. And in addition, I think that there were certain discussions and instructions of this Trial Chamber with regard of the future, I would say, use of the evidences previously introduced on behalf of Mr. Milan Simic, and that was the basis of our position. Because we don't see any particular relevance or link of the evidences and exhibits on behalf of Mr. Milan Simic with regard to the other three defendants. In order to facilitate proceedings, and following the instruction of the Trial Chamber, we decided to simply attach this number of Mr. Milan Simic exhibits on our side. But of course that's final decision would be of this Trial Chamber. Thank you, Your Honour. And also I have another matter to discuss after your ruling. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: To clear the -- what appears to be a misunderstanding on this issue of whether or not exhibits can be used against the three, the position is that all the evidence that was adduced from the beginning of the trial, up until the separation, can be -- is common to all the three accused. After the -- Mr. Milan Simic pled guilty, all the contents of the plea agreement, everything that he said in his statements to the Prosecution or on record, all those will not affect these three accused persons. It is all right for the Defence to choose which exhibits they are going to rely on or which ones they are not going to rely on, but that does not affect the position of the Prosecution or Trial Chamber. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you for your ruling and decision. Now I would like, with the permission of this Trial Chamber, to go into private session, because it's a rather delicate matter with regard to the -- some medical issue of one of the co-accused, and I would kindly ask to go into private session. And I will explain the approach of the Defence with regard to the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go into private session.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned to be followed
